mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for three consecutive months and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month and the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and increases corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases for three consecutive months and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% in a month and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real final sales (RSAFS) also increase by more than 2% over the same month, it signals a strengthening demand side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% and RSAFS by more than 2% in the same month, and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) decreases by more than 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.5% over the same month, it signals a weakening supply side and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 2% and UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 2% and UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in the same month, and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances.
